full_judgment:
Mohammad Ismailuddin Sarker, J: This appeal by the defendant is directed against the judgment and order dated 9.7.88 passed by the learned District judge, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 135 of 1988 rejecting an application under Order 41 rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure as not maintainable. 

 3. Against the aforesaid order dated 1.4.87 passed by the Family Court the defendant appellant filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 118 of 1987 before the Court of the District Judge, Dhaka under section 17(1) of the Family Court Ordinance. The Miscellaneous Appeal was admitted by the learned District Judge and it was fixed for hearing on 4.6.88 on which date a petition for adjournment of hearing of the Miscellaneous Appeal was filed by the defendant-appellant but the petition for adjournment was rejected and the appeal dismissed for default. 

 4. Thereafter on 2.7.88 the appellant filed an application under Order 41 rule 19 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, being Miscellaneous Case No. 135 of 1988, for re-admission of the appeal dismissed for default; and the learned District Judge by the impugned judgment and order dated 9.7.88 rejected the application as not maintainable on the ground that the court of the District Judge being a Family Court under the Family Court Ordinance, the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure (except sections 10 and 11) including the provisions of Order 41 rule 19 are not applicable. 

 According to the learned District Judge, except the provisions of sections 10 and 11, the Code of Civil Procedure is not applicable to the proceedings before the Family Court and the Court of the District Judge being the appellate Court under the said Ordinance the provisions of Order 41 rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure are not applicable to the proceedings in appeals before the court of District Judge. The learned Advocate referred to the case of AKM Ruhul Amin Vs. The District Judge, reported in 38 DLR (AD) 172, wherein interpreting section 29(4) of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Ordinance, 1983 their Lordships of the Appellate Division held that the District Judge means the court of the District Judge even though it is provided in that section that any person aggrieved by a decision of the Election Tribunal may prefer an appeal to the District Judge, within whose jurisdiction the election in dispute was held.
